scope.context: 在项目开发完成后，对 ChordLens 整个代码仓库进行一轮标准代码安全性审查。
limitations: Generated build artifacts and installed dependency bodies were excluded in favor of authoritative source, manifests, and lockfiles.
No online vulnerability-database query was performed.
scope.runtimeStatus: Static source review; no network access or external dependency advisory lookup.
scope.summary: Standard offline source audit of the current ChordLens repository, covering application TypeScript/React, Tauri Rust code and capabilities, the Python Basic Pitch adapter, tests, manifests, and lockfiles.
scope.validationMode: Independent baseline plus two focused investigations, followed by parent source validation.

assets: User-selected local audio files and their filesystem paths
Local song library, transcription state, and SQLite database
Renderer, Python analyzer, and desktop availability
assumptions: The application has one local main window, no network service, no remote capability origin, and no multi-user or tenant boundary
The current React source exposes no HTML/code execution sink and production CSP restricts scripts to self
Users intentionally choose files and approve microphone access, but selected media and exported-recipient context are untrusted
attackerCapabilities: Supply crafted, compressed, long, high-channel-count, or note-dense audio and persuade the local user to import it
Trigger rapid or overlapping local UI actions
Execute JavaScript in the main renderer only after a separate renderer compromise
Receive an analysis JSON that the user explicitly exports and shares
securityObjectives: Bound memory, CPU, process count, decoded work, and output for untrusted media
Stop every microphone track on stop, error, timeout, ownership loss, and unmount
Bind native file analysis to explicit user authorization and least privilege
Prevent stale analysis jobs from corrupting newer song state
Exclude internal filesystem metadata from ordinary portable exports
threatModel.summary: ChordLens is a local-first, single-user macOS Tauri application. Its principal risks arise when user-selected audio and microphone data cross into renderer media APIs or an optional Python analyzer, when renderer code invokes native commands, and when internal local metadata is persisted or exported.
trustBoundaries: Browser or native file picker into the renderer
Renderer JavaScript across Tauri IPC into Rust commands
Rust process supervisor into Python, Basic Pitch, librosa, and media decoders
OS microphone permission into MediaRecorder and application-owned streams
Internal Song persistence model into portable JSON exports
